In [[probability theory]] and [[statistics]], the '''continuous binomial distribution''' (also called the '''cobin distribution''') is a family of continuous probability distributions on the unit interval that belongs to an [[exponential dispersion model|exponential dispersion family]]. It was introduced as a response distribution for [[generalized linear model]]s for continuous proportional data, proposed as an alternative to [[beta regression]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Lee |first=Changwoo J. |last2=Dahl |first2=Benjamin K. |last3=Ovaskainen |first3=Otso |last4=Dunson |first4=David B. |date=2026-05-18 |title=Scalable and robust regression models for continuous proportional data |url=https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13188389/ |journal=Journal of the American Statistical Association |doi=10.1080/01621459.2026.2626081 |issn=0162-1459 |pmc=13188389 |pmid=42169758}}</ref> The special case <math>\lambda=1</math> coincides with the [[continuous Bernoulli distribution]]<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Loaiza-Ganem |first=Gabriel |last2=Cunningham |first2=John |date=2019 |title=The continuous Bernoulli: fixing a pervasive error in variational autoencoders |url=https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper/2019/hash/f82798ec8909d23e55679ee26bb26437-Abstract.html |journal=Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems |publisher=Curran Associates, Inc. |volume=32}}</ref>.

==Definition==
A random variable <math>X</math> is said to follow a continuous binomial (cobin) distribution with natural parameter <math>\theta</math> and inverse dispersion <math>\lambda\in\{1,2,\dots\}</math>, written <math>X\sim\mathrm{cobin}(\theta,\lambda^{-1})</math>, if it has density on <math>[0,1]</math> given by
:<math>
f(x;\theta,\lambda)=h(x;\lambda)\exp\!\big(\lambda\theta x-\lambda B(\theta)\big),\qquad 0\le x\le 1,
</math>
where the log-partition function is
:<math>
B(\theta)=
\begin{cases}
\log\!\left(\frac{e^\theta-1}{\theta}\right), & \theta\ne 0,\\
0, & \theta=0,
\end{cases}
</math>
and the base measure <math>h(x;\lambda)</math> is
:<math>
h(x;\lambda)=\frac{\lambda}{(\lambda-1)!}\sum_{k=0}^{\lambda}(-1)^k{\lambda\choose k}\,\max(0,\lambda x-k)^{\lambda-1},
</math>
with <math>h(x;1)=1</math>. The function <math>h(x;\lambda)/\lambda</math> coincides with the probability density function of the [[Irwin–Hall distribution]] with parameter <math>n=\lambda</math>, evaluated at <math>\lambda x</math>.

When <math>\lambda</math> is fixed, the cobin distribution belongs to a one-parameter [[natural exponential family]] in <math>\theta</math>.

==Related distributions==

* '''Continuous Bernoulli distribution''': when <math>\lambda=1</math>, the cobin distribution reduces to the [[continuous Bernoulli distribution]].

* '''Bates distribution''': when <math>\theta=0</math>, the density reduces to <math>h(x;\lambda)</math>, corresponding to the distribution of the mean of <math>\lambda</math> independent <math>\mathrm{Uniform}(0,1)</math> random variables (equivalently, a scaled [[Irwin–Hall distribution]] or [[Bates distribution]]).

* '''Uniform distribution''': when <math>\lambda=1</math> and <math>\theta=0</math>, the distribution reduces to the [[continuous uniform distribution]] on <math>[0,1]</math>.

* If <math>X_1,\dots,X_\lambda</math> are independent and identically distributed [[Continuous Bernoulli distribution|continuous Bernoulli]] random variables with common natural parameter <math>\theta</math>, then
:<math>
\bar{X}=\frac{1}{\lambda}\sum_{i=1}^{\lambda} X_i
\sim \mathrm{cobin}(\theta,\lambda^{-1}).
</math>

==Properties==

===Mean and variance===
The mean and variance of <math>X\sim\mathrm{cobin}(\theta,\lambda^{-1})</math> can be expressed in terms of derivatives of <math>B(\theta)</math>:

* <math>\operatorname{E}(X)=B'(\theta)=\frac{e^\theta}{e^\theta-1}-\frac{1}{\theta}</math>, for <math>\theta\ne 0</math>.
* <math>\operatorname{Var}(X)=\frac{1}{\lambda}B''(\theta)=\frac{1}{\lambda}\left(\frac{1}{\theta^2}-\frac{e^\theta}{(e^\theta-1)^2}\right)</math>, for <math>\theta\ne 0</math>.

If <math>\theta=0</math>, then <math>\operatorname{E}(X)=\frac{1}{2}</math> and <math>\operatorname{Var}(X)=\frac{1}{12\lambda}</math>.

===Sufficient statistic for the mean===
If <math>X_1,\ldots,X_n</math> are independent and identically distributed continuous binomial random variables with common natural parameter <math>\theta</math> and fixed inverse dispersion parameter <math>\lambda</math>, then the sample mean
:<math>
\bar{X}=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}X_i
</math>
is a sufficient statistic for <math>\theta</math>. 

This is in contrast with the [[Beta distribution|beta distribution]]: under a mean–precision parameterisation <math>X_i\sim\mathrm{Beta}(\mu\phi,(1-\mu)\phi)</math> with fixed <math>\phi</math>, a sufficient statistic for the mean <math>\mu</math> is
:<math>
\sum_{i=1}^{n}\log\!\left(\frac{X_i}{1-X_i}\right),
</math>
not the sample mean <math>
\bar{X}
</math>.

==Applications==
The cobin distribution has been proposed as a response distribution for [[generalized linear model]]s of continuous proportional data, as an alternative to beta regression, including extensions with random effects.
